{'text': "I've noticed lately that Apple seems to have given up on Cinematic mode, and a video experiment perfectly illustrates my disappointment with this fact."}

{'text': "Not because the feature is bad, but because it has come so close to being genuinely usable that it's hard to understand why Apple hasn't taken better advantage of the massive performance gains between the iPhone 13 when it first launched and the latest iPhone. Let me show you…"}

{'text': "I've previously explained why I understand Apple hasn't made updating this feature a priority, but I've also argued that it should, to encourage future videographers and filmmakers — especially young people who may not have access to other camera equipment."}

{'text': "I have a friend who uses his smartphone to interview strangers on the street, and often manages to get them to open up in ways you wouldn't expect. I decided to turn the tables and put him on a stool, then film with a smartphone — this time my iPhone 16 Pro Max."}

{'text': "I wanted to see how complex a scene Cinematic mode could handle: a person sitting in the foreground, with railings roughly 25 feet behind, and the O2 Arena across the river possibly close to a thousand feet away. Add to that the fact that he'd be sitting on a stool, so his range of movement would be quite limited."}

{'text': "The answer is… so close, yet so far. The overall effect is decent, but there's noticeable halation between CK's legs and the railings, and when he moves his head past the O2's support structures, those structures sometimes come into focus. When he opens his hands, the river behind occasionally snaps into focus as well:"}

{'text': "To be fair, CK reckons the average viewer watching the footage probably wouldn't notice the issue. If they're not a filmmaker or a tech-savvy person who understands how this feature works, they might not even pick up on these flaws — and even if they did, they wouldn't find them bothersome. I suspect he might be right."}

{'text': 'But the issue really does bother me, and I think even amateur filmmaking enthusiasts would share the same disappointment — and these people are precisely the target audience for this feature.'}

{'text': "As I said at the start, my disappointment isn't because the feature is bad, but because I genuinely believe that if Apple made proper use of the performance and neural processing capabilities of current iPhone chips, this feature could be dramatically improved. In fact, I'd expect a properly updated Cinematic mode to handle far more challenging scenarios than this one."}

{'text': 'Do you agree with my take? Would you like Apple to take Cinematic mode seriously? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.'}
